title: AI-Assisted Service Management: Triage, Knowledge, and Incident Handoff (2026)

questions.question: What does extract_fields return for the Salesforce v3 billing follow-up ticket in TICKETS?
options: BILLING intent, product salesforce, version v3, prior_contact=True, and full confidence
ACCESS intent, no product, no version, and prior_contact=False
BREAK_FIX intent, product grafana, version v2, and urgency_p1=True
UNKNOWN intent because a follow-up marker suppresses keyword extraction
questions.explanation: The ticket contains invoice and charge terms, Salesforce, v3, and the Re:/Reopening markers. All three completeness fields are filled, so confidence reaches 1.0 and prior_contact is true.

questions.question: The ticket text 'Hi, I need access to something. Thanks.' produces only an access intent. How does route_ticket handle it?
options: ROUTE to Identity & Access Management at 1.00 confidence
ROUTE_FLAG to Identity & Access Management because confidence is 0.60
ESCALATE to L2 because any missing product automatically falls below 0.30
ROUTE_FLAG to General Triage because the access keyword is ignored without a version
questions.explanation: The intent is filled but product and version are not, giving 0.4 + 1/3*0.6 = 0.60. That is above escalation but below the 0.75 route threshold, so the draft is held for review in the access queue.

questions.question: What happens to the ticket reporting a complete production outage with all users locked out?
options: It is routed normally once the product and version are extracted
It is ROUTE_FLAG because urgent tickets need a human draft review
It is ESCALATE to the L2 On-Call queue because a P1 urgency signal takes priority
It is sent to Finance & Billing because the text mentions an SLA breach
questions.explanation: Production down, all users, data loss risk, and SLA breach are P1 signals. route_ticket checks urgency before confidence and sends the ticket directly to L2 On-Call.

questions.question: What verdict does score_response give the good Grafana draft against ARTICLES?
options: PARTIAL, because one step lacks an imperative verb
BLOCK, because retrieved articles cannot ground an operational response
PARTIAL, because five steps exceed the actionability limit
PASS, because all five numbered steps are grounded and imperative
questions.explanation: Each step contains a four-word phrase found in the retrieved articles, and each starts with an allowed imperative without speculative language. Groundedness is 1.0 and actionability is 1.0.

questions.question: Why does the bad Grafana draft receive BLOCK rather than PARTIAL?
options: Its hallucinated step makes groundedness 75%, and any value below 100% blocks the response
It has no numbered steps, so the scorer cannot evaluate it
The draft contains five steps, which exceeds the article-list size
The route threshold of 0.75 is applied to response quality instead of ticket confidence
questions.explanation: The four numbered steps include one invented cache-directory step, so groundedness is 0.75. score_response blocks whenever groundedness is below 1.0; the speculative language is an additional actionability failure.

questions.question: What does score_response return when a draft contains no numbered steps at all?
options: PASS with groundedness 1.0 because there are no unsupported steps
BLOCK with groundedness 0.0, actionability 0.0, and a no-numbered-steps failure
PARTIAL with one implicit step made from the whole paragraph
ROUTE_FLAG because the ticket confidence threshold applies to the draft
questions.explanation: The scorer does not treat an unstructured paragraph as a safely grounded procedure. With no numbered steps it returns BLOCK and identifies the missing structure explicitly.
